note: The demo as a tutorial (GAME_SPEC §13.2), on the interactive bench (data/benches/lab.json). Each step: what to do, why, and checks read from the lab; it is passed when all its checks hold. play: the gestures it asks for, named as Ui::locate names things (the screen points at the last it can find; lab_tests play them all). fails end the run until a reset; goal is checked once every step is passed: the bench's game goals met (GAME_SPEC §13.5), and the totals unchanged.
title: Tutorial: copper from malachite

steps.title: Set out the flask
steps.text: Click the flask in Supplies on the left to pick it up, then click a square of the bench to put it down.
steps.why: Everything happens in this 250 mL flask: first the gas, then the solution, then the crystals.

checks.text: the flask stands on the bench

steps.title: A burner under the flask
steps.text: Pick up the burner in Supplies, then click the flask: it goes under it.
steps.why: A burner heats the vessel it stands under. Chosen, its gas valve shows in the column on the right.

checks.text: the burner is under the flask

steps.title: Bring the malachite
steps.text: Pick up the jar in Supplies, then click a free square of the bench.
steps.why: The jar holds 5 g of malachite, a green copper carbonate mineral, as a powder.

checks.text: the jar stands on the bench

steps.title: Tip the malachite into the flask
steps.text: Pick up the jar, then right-click the flask. In the menu that opens, click "tip in the malachite".
steps.why: Malachite is Cu2CO3(OH)2. Heated, it breaks down into black copper oxide, carbon dioxide and water.

checks.text: all 5 g of malachite in the flask

steps.title: Catch the gas
steps.text: Pick up the balloon in Supplies, then click the flask.
steps.why: The balloon closes the flask's mouth: any gas that leaves the flask now goes into the balloon.

checks.text: the balloon is on the flask

steps.title: Light the burner
steps.text: Right-click the burner to choose it, then drag its valve, in the column on the right, all the way open.
steps.why: The flame is at about 1,900 C; the valve sets how much of its heat reaches the flask.

checks.text: the valve fully open

steps.title: Speed up time
steps.text: Click "600x" at the top. Pause or slow down whenever you like.
steps.why: Every 1/60 s of the lab is still simulated and checked; at 600x ten minutes pass in a second.

checks.text: time runs at least 60 times faster

steps.title: Wait for the malachite to break down
steps.text: Watch the green powder turn black and the balloon grow. Point at the flask to read what is in it.
steps.why: Cu2CO3(OH)2 -> 2 CuO + CO2 + H2O, fast from about 300 C. The balloon takes the flask's hot air first, then the carbon dioxide and the steam.

checks.text: less than 5 mg of malachite left

steps.title: Hand in the balloon
steps.text: Pick up the balloon, then click slot 1 of the outbox, at the bottom: its goal is carbon dioxide in the balloon.
steps.why: Taking it off the flask seals it, with the carbon dioxide inside.

checks.text: the balloon is in slot 1

steps.title: Let the flask cool
steps.text: Choose the burner and shut its valve, then wait for the flask to cool.
steps.why: The black copper oxide stays in the flask for the next stage. Acid on hot glass would spit.

checks.text: the burner is off
the flask below 30 C

steps.title: Bring the acid
steps.text: Pick up the acid in Supplies, then click a free square of the bench.
steps.why: It is about 250 mL of 1 M sulfuric acid, H2SO4 in water.

checks.text: the acid stands on the bench

steps.title: Pour the acid onto the oxide
steps.text: Pick up the acid, then right-click the flask. The menu opens at 50 mL: click "pour". (A left click on the flask pours by hand, while the button is held.)
steps.why: CuO + H2SO4 -> CuSO4 + H2O. About 45 mL reacts all the oxide; a little more makes sure none is left.

checks.text: more than 45 mL of acid in the flask
less than 120 mL (more only takes longer to boil off)

steps.title: Stir
steps.text: Right-click the flask to choose it, then "stir" in the column on the right.
steps.why: It keeps the grains in the acid and the liquid even. The acid reaches them far faster than they can use it, so it is their surface and its warmth that set the pace, not the stirring.

checks.text: the flask is stirred

steps.title: A low flame
steps.text: Choose the burner and set its valve to about a fifth open.
steps.why: Warmth speeds the dissolving. A full flame would boil the acid before it has done its work.

checks.text: the valve at least 10% open
and at most 40%

steps.title: Wait for the oxide to dissolve
steps.text: Watch the black powder disappear and the liquid turn blue.
steps.why: The blue is the copper ion in water, Cu2+(aq): copper sulfate solution.

checks.text: less than 1 mg of copper oxide left

steps.title: Stop stirring
steps.text: Choose the flask and click "stirring" to stop.
steps.why: Its work is done: the oxide is gone. (Stirring would bring the salt to growing crystals faster, but they grow well enough still.)

checks.text: the flask is not stirred

steps.title: The condenser
steps.text: Pick up the condenser in Supplies, then click the flask.
steps.why: Its cold jacket turns the steam from the flask back into liquid water.

checks.text: the condenser is on the flask

steps.title: A beaker for the water
steps.text: Pick up the beaker in Supplies, then click a free square of the bench.

checks.text: the beaker stands on the bench

steps.title: Under the outlet
steps.text: Press the end of the condenser's outlet and drag to the beaker: the outlet runs into it.
steps.why: What condenses runs down into the beaker.

checks.text: the condenser drains into the beaker

steps.title: A monitor
steps.text: Drag a monitor out of the parts drawer, beside the outbox, onto a free square of the bench.
steps.why: Boiling down is the step to watch: too far, and the crystals have nothing to grow from. A monitor watches a value for you while the clock runs fast.

checks.text: a monitor on the bench

steps.title: Let it sense the flask
steps.text: Drag from the monitor's sensing port, the dot at its foot, onto the flask. Its settings open.
steps.why: A monitor reads what it senses: the dashed line from its foot shows what that is.

checks.text: it senses the flask

steps.title: Watch the flask's water
steps.text: Click "a material", then H2O(l), the flask's liquid water, then "mass".
steps.why: The lists hold only what the flask has now: its materials, or the flask's own quantities, such as its temperature.

checks.text: it watches the mass of the water in the flask

steps.title: Below 12 g
steps.text: Click "below". Then click the value, type 12, and click "set".
steps.why: From then on the monitor signals whenever less than 12 g of water is left: its lamp lights, and its port, on its right, sends the signal. With less, the boiling solution would be saturated, and above about 94 C the pale trihydrate comes out of it, not the blue crystals.

checks.text: the monitor signals below 12 g of water

steps.title: Rig it to the burner
steps.text: Drag from the monitor's port, the dot on its right, onto the burner. The rig's settings open.
steps.why: A rig sets a control when its signal changes: here, the burner's valve.

checks.text: a rig from the monitor to the burner's valve

steps.title: Close the valve when it signals
steps.text: On the "when on" row, click the value and type 0. Leave "when off" as it is. Click "rig".
steps.why: When the water goes below 12 g, the valve closes itself, at any speed. Your own hand can still open it after: the control keeps whatever set it last.

checks.text: the burner closes when the monitor signals

steps.title: An alarm
steps.text: Drag an alarm out of the parts drawer onto a free square.
steps.why: An alarm stops the clock when its input turns on, and shows you what set it off.

checks.text: an alarm on the bench

steps.title: Wire the monitor to it
steps.text: Drag from the monitor's port onto the alarm.

checks.text: the monitor wired into the alarm

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Choose the burner and open its valve all the way.
steps.why: Only the water boils off: the copper sulfate and the leftover acid stay in the flask.

checks.text: the valve fully open

steps.title: Boil it down, not dry
steps.text: Speed up as you like: below 12 g of water the monitor closes the valve, and the alarm stops the clock.
steps.why: The crystals need water to grow from. Boiled dry, the salt loses its own water and turns white.

checks.text: less than 12 g of water left in the flask
the rig closed the valve
the alarm rang

steps.title: Let it cool
steps.text: Press play (or a speed) to answer the alarm, and wait.
steps.why: Cold water dissolves less copper sulfate: as the solution cools, blue CuSO4.5H2O crystals grow out of it.

checks.text: the burner is off
the flask below 21 C

steps.title: Let the crystals grow
steps.text: Wait about two hours of the lab's time (at 600x, twelve seconds). Point at the flask: the readout counts the crystals.
steps.why: New crystals start rarely, so they are few, and the salt comes out onto them only as fast as it diffuses to them through the still solution: they grow large, and slowly.

checks.text: more than 8.9 g of crystals

steps.title: Take the condenser off
steps.text: Pick up the condenser off the flask, then click a free square of the bench. Moved away, its outlet no longer drips into the beaker.

checks.text: the condenser is off the flask

steps.title: A beaker for the liquor
steps.text: Pick up the waste beaker in Supplies, then click a free square of the bench.

checks.text: the waste beaker stands on the bench

steps.title: Pour off the liquor
steps.text: Pick up the flask, then right-click the waste beaker. Drag the menu's slider to the right end, then click "pour it all".
steps.why: The liquor holds the leftover acid and the copper sulfate still dissolved. Poured off, it leaves the crystals clean.

checks.text: no liquid left in the flask

steps.title: Hand in the water
steps.text: Pick up the beaker, then click slot 2: pure water in the beaker.

checks.text: the beaker is in slot 2

steps.title: Hand in the crystals
steps.text: Pick up the flask, then click slot 3: the crystals. The burner stays on the bench.

checks.text: the flask is in slot 3

fails.text: The balloon burst: it took more gas than its 3 L. Press reset to start again.
The acid went in before the malachite had broken down. Under the liquid it never gets hot enough to. Press reset to start again.
The crystals overheated: they lost their water of crystallisation and turned to white copper sulfate. Press reset to start again.
The balloon was handed in before it held the carbon dioxide. Press reset to start again.
The beaker was handed in holding more than water. Press reset to start again.
The flask was handed in with its liquor: the crystals are not clean. Press reset to start again.
The flask was handed in without its crystals. Press reset to start again.
Only the balloon, the beaker of water and the flask of crystals go in the outbox. Press reset to start again.

goal.text: goal met: carbon dioxide in the balloon (slot 1)
goal met: pure water in the beaker (slot 2)
goal met: copper sulfate crystals, 99.9% pure (slot 3)
every element, mass and energy unchanged
